title: Getting On and Off: felszáll, leszáll

sections.title: A surface, not a space
sections.content: Hungarian treats a bus, tram or metro as a surface you climb onto, not a space you go into — that's why *felszáll* ("get on") uses -ra/-re, the same "onto" case from looking for a flat, and *leszáll* ("get off") uses -ról/-ről, "off of": *Felszállok* a buszra. ("I get on the bus.") *Leszállok* a *következő* *megállónál*. ("I get off at the next stop." — here *megálló* takes -nál/-nél, "at", since you're naming the stop, not the vehicle. With the vehicle itself it is -ról/-ről: *Leszállok* a *buszról*. "I get off the bus.")

items.spanish: Felszállok a villamosra a Blaha Lujza téren.
items.english: I get on the tram at Blaha Lujza Square.
I get off at the next stop.

sections.content: *felszáll* and *leszáll* are verbal-prefix pairs (*fel*- "up", *le*- "down") — in a question, the prefix and the verb can split apart: Hol *szállsz* *le*?, not Hol *leszállsz*?. You met this splitting of prefix and verb in the cooking unit (a2-49); here it just comes back.
